title: BI deports 139 Indonesian fugitives
summary: The Bureau of Immigration (BI) deported 139 Indonesian fugitives on Tuesday, citing threats they posed to national security and public interest.

blocks.text: The Bureau of Immigration (BI) deported 139 Indonesian fugitives on Tuesday, citing threats they posed to national security and public interest.
In a press release, the BI said the deportees were scheduled to leave the country aboard a chartered flight from the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 3.
The group consisted of 111 men and 28 women who had previously been held in the custody of the Philippine National Police (PNP).

“The deportees ... were identified as fugitives by Indonesian authorities and subsequently classified as undesirable aliens under Philippine immigration laws for posing threats to national security and public interest,” the BI said.
The BI Board of Commissioners issued a Summary Deportation Order against the group on Nov. 19.
The order was implemented through coordination among the BI, the PNP Aviation Security Group and the Indonesian Embassy.
BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado said the bureau would continue expediting the deportation of foreign fugitives to protect the country's security and public interest.

Editorial note: The original copy says the deportation was completed but later says the deportees were merely scheduled to leave. Confirm whether the chartered flight had already departed before publication.— MCG, GMA News
